stapel-chat.note: release v0.8.6 - 2026-09-06: leaving is UNDOABLE, and a thread you left finally has a listing. 0.8.5 gave a person a way out of a thread and no way back into it, so somebody who pressed «Leave conversation» by mistake could reach the thread only by a URL they had kept - the gap chat-react carried as its one open upstream ask. Two wire surfaces move and both are what @stapel/chat-react regenerates against. GET /conversations gains `left=true`, the EXACT COMPLEMENT of the default list: services.left_of is written as the negation of services.inbox_of, so every thread a person is party to is on exactly one of the two and none can fall between them. It is ordered by WHEN THE CALLER LEFT, newest departure first, which is why `anchor` on this list is a left_at where the inbox's is an updated_at - a cursor from one list means nothing on the other, and the pair therefore gives the left view its OWN query key rather than sharing the inbox's. `search`, `unread` and the paging trio compose exactly as they do on the inbox, over the same filter_inbox. POST /conversations/{id}/rejoin -> 204 is the way back, and clearing the caller's left_at is the entire verb: read markers are untouched (the thread comes back with the badge it had) and so is updated_at (it comes back where the departure left it, not at the top of the inbox), it is idempotent, no participant row is created, and a non-party gets 403 error.403.chat_not_participant - the same key GET and DELETE on that thread already give them. No system line is posted on the way back, deliberately: a departure is announced because the counterpart faces silence they cannot explain, a return is a person undoing their own mistake. ConversationResponse gains a TOP-LEVEL left_at (the requesting user's own departure, nullable, and NOT in the schema's required list, so a 0.8.5 body reads as "nobody has left" rather than as a broken contract); it is null on every row of the default list and never null on ?left=true. One consequence of the UNCHANGED search rule, worth stating because it looks like a bug and is not: a left thread's last line is the departure marker, and an unlabelled marker draws nothing and is found by nothing (drawn_last_line, one rule for the preview and the search), so ?left=true&search= finds these rows by the counterpart's name and the subject card's title, never by the last thing anyone said in them. docs/errors.json is BYTE-IDENTICAL across 0.8.5..0.8.6 - the one refusal already existed - so gen:errors regenerates unchanged and no locale bundle shifts; docs/schema.json and docs/capabilities.json are what move. release v0.8.5 - 2026-09-06: a person can LEAVE a conversation, and leaving deletes nothing. DELETE /chat/api/v1/conversations/{id} answered 405 until this release - there was no way off a thread at all - and now answers 204: the caller's participant row is stamped left_at, the thread drops off THEIR list, unread counts and ?search=, their live subscription is revoked, and a system line records it in the transcript as chat.participant.left:<user_id>. It is not a delete: every message stays, the other party keeps the thread untouched, the leaver still reaches their own history by id, and any AUTHORED message from the other side clears the marker and brings the thread back (a system line resurfaces nobody, including the departure line itself). Idempotent - a second DELETE is another 204 and writes no second line - and a non-participant gets the module's one membership refusal, error.403.chat_not_participant, the same answer GET on that URL gives them. Two wire surfaces move and both are what @stapel/chat-react regenerates against: the new delete operation on /conversations/{conversation_id}, and ParticipantResponse.left_at (nullable date-time, NOT in the schema's required list, so a body from a 0.8.4 server reads as "nobody has left" rather than as a broken contract). docs/errors.json is BYTE-IDENTICAL across 0.8.4..0.8.5 - the refusal already existed - so gen:errors regenerates unchanged and no locale bundle shifts; docs/schema.json and docs/capabilities.json are what move. The module owns no WORDS for the marker (STAPEL_CHAT["SYSTEM_LINE_LABELS"] is empty out of the box and the id after the colon is there so a client can name the person without this module inventing a sentence in a language it does not own) - the pair renders it. release v0.8.4 - 2026-09-06: the null on an inbox row says WHICH null it is. LastMessageResponse gains `preview_reason` — deleted | attachment | system, or null when the line has words — decided server-side by services.last_line_reason over the same columns drawn_last_line already reads (docs/capabilities.json and docs/capabilities.meta.json carry it as a gate_function, instead_of Message.deleted_at). This is the follow-up 0.8.3's note named and chat-react's MODULE.md carried: inboxPreviewLine guessed from `kind`, so a tombstone and an attachment-only message arrived as one `null` and the row drew «Attachment» over a deletion. The dormant `chat.list.preview_deleted` copy the pair has shipped since it had an inbox is reachable at this pin and the guess is deleted rather than kept beside it. docs/errors.json is BYTE-IDENTICAL across 0.8.3..0.8.4 (no new refusal), so gen:errors regenerates unchanged and no locale bundle shifts; docs/schema.json and the two capabilities files are what move.
